body: There is no `searchAsYouType` option in Vue

Problem is they are handled differently, in IS.js it adds the `autofocus` attribute but for some reason jsdom does not focus it so we have to test the attribute rather than `toHaveFocus`. (actually it's not implemented : https://github.com/jsdom/jsdom/issues/3041)
For React, [it doesn't get added to the list of attributes](https://github.com/facebook/react/blob/34de2986dfeddda31cb76d298c6d59b271d976fa/packages/react-dom-bindings/src/client/ReactDOMComponent.js#L636-L641) but [it gets polyfilled](https://github.com/facebook/react/blob/34de2986dfeddda31cb76d298c6d59b271d976fa/packages/react-dom-bindings/src/client/ReactFiberConfigDOM.js#L673-L678) to be focused imperatively on commit so here we can only test with `toHaveFocus` 🫠
Oof 😅. ~~Thanks for digging into this! Let's keep it like that.~~ I saw you figured out a way to handle both behaviors 👏 .
If we're really strict about it, this is breaking. A CSS rule targeting the element by `title` would no longer work.

body: I don't think we need those component tests anymore. In the other common test suite PRs we've only kept the ones in React InstantSearch for when we create an `instantsearch-vdom` package in the future. The ones in InstantSearch.js should go away as they only test an internal API that's covered by our widget tests.
As per my other comment, I think we can get rid of this.

In this file you could merge the tests from `search-box-test.ts`. You can check the previously merged common test suite PRs to see what's usually migrated — what should be enough to have is as "options" `describe` block with the following tests:

- "throws without a `container`"
- "adds custom CSS classes"
Removing attributes from the markup is technically breaking, as users may be targeting them with CSS or even custom JavaScript.
I don't think the prop changes on this PR should block us, as long as we provide consistent class names that are consistent and well documented, for customers to rely on.
